benefits.heading: How Pharmacy First Can Help
benefits.body: Pharmacy First is a community pharmacy pathway that lets a pharmacist assess eligible common conditions when symptoms fit the Pharmacy First pathway. Treatment is supplied only where pathway criteria are met; otherwise you receive advice or referral. The service is designed to give a clear outcome in one visit: treatment where appropriate, practical self-care guidance, or a safe referral when pharmacy care is not enough. Patients from your area can call ahead to confirm whether a consultation is available before travelling.

howItWorks.heading: What Happens During The Consultation
howItWorks.body: Your visit follows a structured consultation so decisions are clinically safe and clearly explained. You will be asked about when symptoms started, what you have already tried, and which medicines you take. The pharmacist explains what can be managed under the pathway and what falls outside it. Where treatment is suitable, you leave with clear instructions; where it is not, you leave with next-step advice rather than uncertainty. Bring a medicines list if you can, and mention allergies, pregnancy or breastfeeding early in the conversation. If you need to check how the service is arranged availability or booking options first, call .

howItWorks.heading: What Happens During The Consultation
howItWorks.body: The consultation is a private, structured conversation shaped around your symptoms and day-to-day context in your area. You will cover what has already been tried, current medicines and whether pharmacy treatment is clinically suitable. If treatment is appropriate, dosing and safety advice are explained clearly. If it is not, the pharmacist still gives practical guidance on GP, NHS 111 or urgent care. Telephone if you need to check consultation availability around family or work schedules.

howItWorks.heading: What Happens During The Consultation
howItWorks.body: The visit is designed to be efficient: gather the key clinical facts, decide the safest outcome, and explain what to do next. Have a medicines list ready and note when symptoms started so the review moves quickly. You may receive treatment where pathway criteria are met, or advice and referral where they are not. That clarity is the point of the consultation for busy patients travelling from your area. Call if you want to check how the service is arranged or booking options first.

howItWorks.heading: What Happens During The Consultation

trustSafety.heading: When To Contact A GP, NHS 111 Or Emergency Services
trustSafety.body: Contact your GP, NHS 111, or urgent care if symptoms are persistent beyond expected recovery, keep worsening despite pharmacy advice, or suggest a more serious infection. Seek urgent medical care for breathing difficulties, chest pain, severe dehydration, confusion, a non-blanching rash, or any emergency symptoms that make you feel critically unwell. Pharmacy pathways are for defined minor illnesses only — if you are pregnant, caring for a very young child outside pathway age limits, or already under active GP review for the same problem, arrange medical assessment instead. If you are unsure after symptoms start in your area, call before travelling and ask whether a Pharmacy First consultation is appropriate today.

trustSafety.heading: When To Contact A GP, NHS 111 Or Emergency Services
trustSafety.body: Pharmacy care supports common community presentations, but it is not the right service for every illness in your area. Return to your GP, NHS 111 or urgent care when symptoms persist, worsen, or suggest a more serious infection. Seek urgent medical care for breathing difficulties, chest pain, severe dehydration, confusion, a non-blanching rash, or any emergency symptoms that make you feel critically unwell. Pregnancy, very young children outside pathway age limits, or problems already under active GP review usually need medical assessment instead. Call if you want help deciding whether Pharmacy First is suitable before you visit.

trustSafety.heading: When To Contact A GP, NHS 111 Or Emergency Services
trustSafety.body: A convenient pharmacy visit is only useful when the pathway still fits. Choose GP, NHS 111 or urgent care instead when symptoms are escalating, unusually severe, or clearly outside Pharmacy First. Seek urgent medical care for breathing difficulties, chest pain, severe dehydration, confusion, a non-blanching rash, or any emergency symptoms that make you feel critically unwell. If speed matters but suitability is unclear, a short call to can prevent an unnecessary trip from your area.

trustSafety.heading: When To Contact A GP, NHS 111 Or Emergency Services
trustSafety.body: Do not make the journey from your area if symptoms already look more serious than a community pharmacy pathway. Seek urgent medical care for breathing difficulties, chest pain, severe dehydration, confusion, a non-blanching rash, or any emergency symptoms that make you feel critically unwell. Contact your GP, NHS 111 or urgent care when symptoms keep worsening, fail to improve as expected, or sit outside Pharmacy First criteria. If you are unsure before travelling, call and ask whether a pharmacy consultation is appropriate today.

mythVsFact.heading: Common Misconceptions
mythVsFact.body: Pharmacy First supports eligible common conditions — it does not replace urgent care for serious illness.
bullets: Myth: Every illness can be managed under Pharmacy First. Fact: Only defined pathway conditions are in scope.
Myth: Pharmacy care replaces emergency services. Fact: Severe or emergency symptoms need urgent medical care.
Myth: Suitability is assumed from your location. Fact: The pharmacist confirms suitability during assessment.
